newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle market at standstill-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle market at standstill-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were at a standstill early Friday following sales this week at $63.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from last week, feedlot sources said.
There were no reported bids, but owners were pricing cattle $63.00 to $64.00, they said. Few sales were expected going into the weekend, the sources said.
Showlists were nearly sold out in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and Kansas.
Weekly sales in the Panhandle totalled about 104,000 head and weekly movement in Kansas was near 94,500.
With the wheat harvest underway but stalled in Kansas and Oklahoma, there has been talk among several feedlot managers that prices could be attractive enough to include in feed rations.
"They're trying to get it cut, but the rain has slowed harvest down, but I think the price is awful close to being able to make it work," one Kansas feedlot source said.
Inexpensive wheat can lower feed costs and make it easier for feedlots to weather outlooks for lower fed cattle prices in the summer as cattle supplies expand, the sources said.
